mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 800,000 units signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decline below 800,000 units does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO rise > 1% MoM does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY is above 2%, the combination signals a potential stagflationary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent stagflationary conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) decline by more than 1% MoM and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3% in the same month, it signals a weakening consumer demand and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines > 1% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.3%
regime_hint: consumer demand and labor market weakness
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of RSAFS decline and UNRATE rise does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4% signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in a regime of high inflation.
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with high inflation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances with FEDFUNDS > 4% despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS > 4% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed in high inflation regimes.
